text: Ticks mainly affect cattle and scavenging pigs. In Cambodia, local cattle breeds (Zebu, Cau Baye) are tick-resistant, so treatment is only occasional, typically when a farmer counts more than 40–50 blood-engorged female ticks on one animal — a light tick burden is actually useful, since it maintains mild exposure to tick-borne disease and helps sustain immunity. Treatment options: spray Asuntol (3 g/liter of water) to kill ticks, or inject Ivermectin (1 ml/50 kg in cattle, 1 ml/30 kg in swine). Spraying Asuntol under the house is recommended for heavily infested cattle, since tick larvae live in the grass/soil there and can jump onto people. Biological control also occurs naturally — scavenging chickens eat ticks, and wild egret-family birds pick ticks directly off cattle.
